prompts.article:
You write customer support articles for Halvard Home, an invented maker of home appliances.
Write one support article about the product and topic below. Start with a short title line,
then the article, 100 to 140 words, in plain UK English. The article must state one specific,
concrete fact clearly, such as a setting, a duration, a figure, a step, or a cause, so a
reader could answer a question from it. Do not mention any error code or part number other
than one given below.

articles.text:
Resetting your Ashby tumble dryer

On the Ashby tumble dryer, E-2194 means a factory reset was interrupted before the saved settings could be cleared. Your previous preferences may still be active.

To try the reset again:

1. Switch the dryer off, unplug it and wait five minutes.
2. Check that the drum is empty, then close the door.
3. Plug the dryer back in and switch it on without selecting a programme.
4. Press and hold the Temperature and Delay Start buttons together for ten seconds.
5. Release both buttons when the display shows “Reset”, then wait until the programme selection screen returns.

A completed reset clears saved drying preferences and delayed starts. If the warning returns, stop repeating the reset and contact Halvard Home support.

Child lock warning on your Orrin heat pump

On the Orrin heat pump, E-1294 means the child lock button has been detected as continuously pressed, so the control panel remains locked. Moisture or dirt on the touch panel can cause this warning.

To clear it:

- Remove anything resting against the control panel.
- Wipe the panel with a soft, dry cloth. Do not spray cleaner directly onto it.
- Make sure your hands are dry, then press and hold the child lock button for five seconds.

When the lock symbol disappears, the controls are available again. The heat pump keeps its previous heating setting while locked.

If the warning returns, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the casing or attempt to repair the controls yourself.

Keel washing machine: child lock will not release

On the Halvard Home Keel washing machine, E-4194 means the child lock has failed to release after you switched it off. The control buttons remain locked because the machine has not confirmed that the lock is disabled.

To reset the child lock:

1. Press and hold the Child Lock button for three seconds.
2. If the lock symbol stays lit, switch the machine off at the socket and unplug it for two minutes.
3. Reconnect the power, switch the machine on, then hold Child Lock for three seconds again.

The child lock disables the controls; it does not indicate whether the door is safe to open. Never force the door. If the controls remain locked, contact Halvard Home support.

articles.topic: the app not finding the device
articles.text:
Ashby tumble dryer not appearing in the app

If the Halvard Home app cannot find your Ashby tumble dryer, its Wi-Fi module may be stuck in standby. This prevents the dryer from broadcasting its setup signal.

KX-9283 is the part number for the Ashby’s Wi-Fi module, which connects the dryer to the app.

Try these steps:
- Switch the dryer off at the socket for 60 seconds, then switch it back on.
- Connect your phone to your home’s 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.
- Hold the dryer’s Wi-Fi button for five seconds, until its light flashes.
- Open the app and select “Add appliance”.

If the dryer still does not appear, contact Halvard Home support and describe the discovery problem. Do not open the casing or replace the module yourself.

Moving your Brio kettle safely

Before moving your Brio kettle, unplug it, empty all water and let it cool completely. Lift the kettle off its base and dry both items before packing.

Check that the lid closes securely. A loose lid latch can allow the lid to spring open during transport. KX-2983 is the replacement lid latch for the Brio kettle. If the latch is cracked or the lid will not stay shut, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support to arrange replacement. Do not tape the lid shut and continue boiling water.

Wrap the kettle and base separately in soft packing material. Keep both upright in a sturdy box, and never carry the kettle by its cable or lid.

Lumen thermostat child lock

The child lock stops children changing the temperature using the Lumen smart thermostat’s screen. To switch it on, press and hold the padlock symbol for five seconds. A closed padlock confirms that the screen controls are locked. Repeat this step to unlock them.

If the lock switches off without anyone touching the screen, a faulty touch sensor may be registering an unlock command.

KX-1283 is the replacement touch-panel assembly for this product, including the sensor that detects child lock commands. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange inspection and, if needed, replacement. Do not open the thermostat yourself.

Until the fault is fixed, do not rely on the child lock to prevent temperature changes.

Vale fridge freezer: unusual vibration

On the Vale fridge freezer, E-7084 means the vibration sensor has detected excessive movement while the compressor is running. An uneven position or contact with nearby furniture can trigger this fault.

To check the appliance:

- Switch it off at the socket and unplug it.
- Check that bottles, shelves and drawers are secure.
- Make sure the cabinet is not touching a wall or cupboard.
- Check that the fridge freezer stands level. Adjust the front levelling feet if needed, without tipping the appliance.
- Leave it unplugged for five minutes, then reconnect it.

If the vibration or warning returns, contact Halvard Home support. An internal compressor mounting may need attention. Do not remove the rear cover or attempt to tighten internal components.

Updating your Mira robot vacuum

On the Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum, error E-7804 means the firmware download was interrupted before installation could begin. Your vacuum is still using its previous firmware.

To retry the update:

1. Place Mira on its charging dock and leave the dock switched on.
2. Check that your home Wi-Fi is working and that Mira shows as connected in the Halvard Home app.
3. Open Mira’s settings in the app, select ‘Firmware update’, then tap ‘Retry’.
4. Keep the vacuum docked and your router switched on until the app confirms the update is complete.

If the update fails again, close and reopen the app, then retry once. Contact Halvard Home support if the problem continues.

articles.topic: the app not finding the device
articles.text:
Brio kettle not appearing in the app

On the Brio kettle, E-7484 means the wireless pairing window has expired, so the app can no longer discover the kettle. This is a connection issue, not a heating fault.

To reconnect:

1. Place the kettle on its powered base, but do not start boiling.
2. Press and hold the wireless button for five seconds, until its light flashes blue.
3. Open the Halvard Home app and select **Add device** within two minutes.
4. Keep your phone within one metre of the kettle until pairing finishes.

If the kettle still does not appear, enable Bluetooth on your phone and allow the app to find nearby devices. Close and reopen the app, then repeat the pairing steps.

Pairing your Orrin heat pump with a voice assistant

If your voice assistant cannot find your Orrin heat pump, its voice pairing module may have stopped responding. This fault can prevent linking even when control through the Halvard Home app still works.

KX-3107 is the part number for the Orrin’s voice pairing module, not an error message. Try resetting its pairing connection before seeking a repair:

1. Open the Halvard Home app and select your heat pump.
2. Go to Settings, then Voice control, and select Reset pairing.
3. Wait 30 seconds, then select Pair voice assistant.
4. Follow the instructions to link your account again.

If pairing still fails, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the heat pump or attempt to replace the module yourself.

Lumen smart thermostat warranty

Your Halvard Home Lumen smart thermostat has a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. It covers manufacturing faults during normal household use.

KX-3170 is the part number identifying this thermostat. Quote it when contacting Halvard Home support so we can check the correct product’s warranty.

For example, if the display repeatedly goes blank while the thermostat still has power, an internal manufacturing fault may be responsible. Contact support with your proof of purchase, purchase date and a brief description of when the problem occurs.

Do not open the casing or attempt an internal repair. Support will assess the fault and explain the next steps. Accidental damage and normal wear are not covered.

Keel washing machine not switching on

If your Keel washing machine shows no lights and does not respond to the power button, start by checking its power supply.

Make sure the plug is firmly inserted and the wall socket is switched on. Test the socket with a working lamp. If the lamp does not light, have the socket checked by a qualified electrician.

Unplug the washing machine for 60 seconds, then reconnect it and try again.

KX-3100 is the Keel’s internal power switch module. A failed module can stop power reaching the controls, leaving the display dark.

If the socket works but the machine remains off, unplug it and contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection. Do not remove the casing or attempt to replace the module yourself.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Tessa dishwasher: water not draining

On your Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, E-6076 means water has remained in the base for more than three minutes after draining started. A blocked filter or kinked drain hose is the usual cause.

Switch the dishwasher off and unplug it before checking anything. If the water is hot, leave it to cool. Place towels around the door, then remove the bottom basket. Lift out the filter, rinse it under running water and refit it securely.

Check any visible section of the drain hose for kinks, without pulling out the appliance or disconnecting pipes.

Restore power and run a drain programme. If the fault returns or water remains, stop using the dishwasher and contact Halvard Home support.

Descaling your Tessa dishwasher

On the Tessa dishwasher, E-6067 means limescale is restricting water flow through the heater, so the water is taking too long to reach the wash temperature.

To descale your dishwasher:

1. Cancel the programme, switch off the dishwasher and let it cool.
2. Remove all dishes and cutlery, then check and clean the filter.
3. Add a dishwasher-safe descaler, following the quantity and placement instructions on its packaging.
4. Switch the dishwasher back on and run an empty programme at 60°C, unless the descaler instructions specify otherwise.

Do not add detergent or mix the descaler with other cleaning products.

If the warning returns after descaling, stop using the dishwasher and contact Halvard Home support. The heater or water pathway may need inspection.

Water leaking underneath your Ashby tumble dryer

On the Ashby tumble dryer, E-6876 means the condensate drain pump is blocked. Water cannot reach the collection tank, so it can build up in the base and leak underneath.

Stop the programme and switch off the dryer. Unplug it only if the plug, socket and surrounding area are dry. If they are wet, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit instead.

Once the power is disconnected, wipe up the water and empty the collection tank. Do not remove the dryer’s panels or try to clear the pump yourself.

Leave the dryer switched off and contact Halvard Home support to arrange a repair. Tell them that water is leaking underneath and that the display shows a drain pump fault.

Descaling your Ashby tumble dryer

Limescale can block the water collection tank’s filter, causing your Ashby tumble dryer to stop and show a full-tank warning even when the tank is empty.

KX-3673 is the removable filter inside the water collection tank. If it has a white, chalky coating, descale it as follows:

1. Switch off the dryer, unplug it and leave it to cool for 30 minutes.
2. Remove and empty the water collection tank, then lift out the filter.
3. Soak the filter in a descaler approved for tumble dryer filters, following the descaler’s dilution and soaking instructions.
4. Rinse thoroughly, then refit the filter and tank.

Do not pour descaler into the dryer. If the warning returns after cleaning, contact Halvard Home support.

Replacing a lower basket wheel

If your Tessa dishwasher’s lower basket tilts or catches when you pull it out, a cracked basket wheel may be the cause.

For the Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, KX-6373 is the replacement lower basket wheel kit. Order this kit from Halvard Home support if a wheel is cracked or missing.

Switch off and unplug the dishwasher before fitting the replacement. Let the appliance cool, empty the lower basket, then lift it out onto a flat surface. Unclip the damaged wheel and press the new wheel onto the same mounting point until it clicks into place.

Refit the basket and slide it fully in and out twice. If it still catches, stop using it and contact support.

Descaling your Orrin heat pump

Limescale can build up inside the domestic hot water heat exchanger, restricting water flow and making the cylinder take longer to heat. This is more likely in hard water areas.

KX-9673 is the descaling service kit for the Orrin heat pump’s hot water heat exchanger. If hot water recovery has become noticeably slower, ask a qualified heating engineer to check for scale and use this kit if descaling is needed.

Do not pour kettle descaler into the cylinder or heating circuit. Keep the casing closed and leave chemical cleaning to the engineer.

After servicing, allow one complete hot water heating cycle before checking performance. If heating remains slow, arrange a further inspection rather than repeating descaling.

Recycling your Fenwick cooker hood

E-6292 means your Fenwick cooker hood has detected an electrical insulation fault in its fan motor. Stop using the hood and switch off its electricity supply. Have a qualified electrician assess the fault before deciding whether to repair or recycle the unit.

If you choose recycling, ask the electrician to disconnect any fixed wiring and make the supply safe before removal. Do not cut cables or dismantle the motor yourself.

Take the old hood to a household waste recycling centre that accepts electrical appliances, or ask your replacement appliance retailer about collection. Check acceptance and booking requirements before travelling.

Do not put the hood in your general rubbish bin. Keep it dry and securely stored until collection or transport.

Connecting your Orrin heat pump to wi-fi

On the Orrin heat pump, E-6922 means the heat pump has tried to join a 5 GHz wi-fi network, which it does not support. Use a 2.4 GHz network instead.

To connect:

1. Check your router settings and make sure the 2.4 GHz network is switched on.
2. If both bands share a network name, follow your router’s instructions to give them separate names.
3. On the heat pump’s control panel, open Settings, then Wi-fi, and select the 2.4 GHz network.
4. Enter your wi-fi password carefully, including any capital letters.

Wait one minute for the connection to complete. If it still fails, restart your router and try again. Contact Halvard Home support if the same message returns.

Timer will not start

On the Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum, E-6232 means the delay start has been cancelled because the vacuum’s internal clock is not set. This can happen after the battery has been completely drained.

To restore the timer, place the vacuum on its charging dock and leave it switched on. Open the Halvard Home app, select your Mira, then go to Settings > Date and time. Choose “Sync with phone” and save.

Next, open the timer menu and set a new start time at least five minutes ahead. The cancelled timer will not restart automatically.

If the message returns, switch the vacuum off for 30 seconds, switch it on again and repeat the clock sync. Contact Halvard Home support if the fault continues.

Moving your Mira robot vacuum

Before moving your Mira robot vacuum, stop cleaning, switch it off and empty the dustbin. Carry the unit level with both hands underneath it; do not lift it by the bumper.

KX-6507 is the removable transport clip that holds the Mira’s front bumper steady during travel. Fit it before packing the switched-off vacuum in its original box, then remove it before switching the vacuum on again.

If the Mira repeatedly reverses after transport, the clip may still be fitted, preventing the bumper from moving freely. Switch the vacuum off, remove the clip and gently check that the bumper presses in and springs back. If it remains stuck, contact Halvard Home support before using the vacuum.

Brio kettle: power cut during use

If a power cut interrupts boiling, switch off your Brio kettle at the socket and unplug it. Wait until the electricity supply is stable before trying again.

A sudden interruption can leave the kettle’s power switch stuck in the off position. To check, let the kettle cool for 10 minutes, then make sure the water is between the minimum and maximum marks. Plug it directly into a wall socket and try switching it on once.

If the switch will not stay on, stop using the kettle. KX-5607 is the replacement power switch module for this product. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange inspection and, if needed, replacement by a qualified technician. Do not open the kettle yourself.

Moving your Lumen smart thermostat

Before moving your Lumen smart thermostat, switch off power to the heating system at the mains. If you need to disconnect wiring, ask a qualified installer to remove and refit the unit.

KX-6505 is the replacement mounting backplate for this product. Check the backplate after transport: a cracked retaining clip can stop the thermostat sitting securely, causing the display to flicker as its contacts lose connection.

If a clip is cracked, do not tape the thermostat in place. Arrange for the backplate to be replaced before restoring power.

For transport, wrap the detached thermostat in soft padding and place it in a rigid box. Keep it dry, and avoid packing heavy objects on top.

Power cut during use

On the Orrin heat pump, E-5107 means mains power was interrupted while the compressor was running. The heat pump has paused operation to protect the compressor during restart.

When power returns, leave the heat pump connected and wait five minutes before trying to restart it. Then press the power button once on the controller and select your usual heating setting. Do not repeatedly switch the electricity supply off and on, as this can interrupt the restart delay.

If the message remains or heating does not resume, switch the heat pump off using its controller and contact Halvard Home support. Tell the adviser that the fault appeared after a power cut. Do not open the casing or attempt electrical repairs.

Corra induction hob: child lock fault

On the Corra induction hob, E-5170 means the child lock touch control has remained active for more than 10 seconds. Moisture, grease or an object resting on the control can cause this fault and prevent the child lock from releasing.

Remove anything covering the control panel. With dry hands, switch the hob off at its wall isolator and allow the surface to cool. Wipe the controls with a soft, dry cloth, then leave the power off for 60 seconds.

Restore the power and touch and hold the lock symbol for three seconds to release the child lock.

If the fault returns, stop using the hob and contact Halvard Home support. Do not attempt to open the hob or repair its controls.

Strange noises from your Corra induction hob

A gentle hum or buzz during cooking is normal, especially at high power. However, a loud rattling or scraping sound needs attention.

On the Corra induction hob, E-1107 means the cooling fan cannot turn freely, usually because its airflow is obstructed. Stop cooking and switch the hob off at the wall isolator. Leave it switched off for at least 10 minutes.

Once the hob has cooled, check that accessible ventilation openings are clear of objects or loose debris. Do not remove covers or put anything into the vents.

Restore power and try the hob once. If the noise or warning returns, switch it off again and contact Halvard Home support. Do not continue using it.

Cleaning the Fenwick cooker hood filter

KX-3926 is the washable metal grease filter for the Fenwick cooker hood. If cooking smells linger and extraction seems weaker than usual, grease blocking the filter mesh may be the cause.

Switch off the hood at the mains and let it cool before cleaning. Support the filter with one hand, release its retaining catch and lower it carefully.

Soak the filter in warm water with washing-up liquid for 15 minutes. Gently brush away grease using a soft brush, then rinse thoroughly. Avoid abrasive cleaners and do not bend the mesh.

Leave the filter to dry completely before refitting it. Make sure the catch locks securely, then restore power. If extraction remains weak, contact Halvard Home support.

Slow draining on your Keel washing machine

If your Keel washing machine takes longer than usual to finish a cycle or leaves clothes unusually wet, a blocked drain filter may be restricting water flow.

KX-3962 is the drain pump filter for this product. A build-up of lint, coins or hair in this filter can cause slow draining and delay the final spin.

To clean it, switch the machine off and unplug it. Allow any hot water to cool. Place towels and a shallow tray beneath the lower front access flap, then loosen the filter slowly to release trapped water.

Remove debris, rinse the filter and refit it securely. Run a drain cycle. If draining remains slow or you notice a leak, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Booking a Keel engineer visit

For the Halvard Home Keel washing machine, KX-3928 identifies the drain pump housing. A crack in this housing can cause water to leak beneath the machine during draining. Stop using the machine if you notice this fault.

Switch the machine off and close its water supply tap. Unplug it only if the plug and surrounding area are dry and safe to reach. Do not remove panels or attempt to seal the leak yourself.

Contact Halvard Home customer support to book an engineer visit. Have your machine’s serial number, address and preferred appointment dates ready. Describe where the water appears and mention the part reference above. The engineer will inspect the leak and confirm whether the housing needs replacing.

Connecting your Tessa dishwasher to wi-fi

On the Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, E-3865 means the appliance has detected a 5 GHz wi-fi network, which it cannot join. The dishwasher needs a 2.4 GHz connection.

Open your router’s settings and check that its 2.4 GHz network is switched on. If your router gives each band a separate network name, connect your phone to the 2.4 GHz network before restarting dishwasher setup in the Halvard Home app.

Keep your phone near the dishwasher during setup and enter your wi-fi password carefully. Passwords are case-sensitive.

If the connection still fails, restart your router, wait two minutes, then try again. Contact Halvard Home support if the same message returns after these checks.

Ashby tumble dryer: child lock

On the Ashby tumble dryer, E-3685 means the child lock cannot be released because the dryer has detected a control button being held down. This can happen if an object presses against the control panel or a button sticks.

To clear the fault:

1. Switch the dryer off and unplug it. Wait two minutes.
2. Remove anything touching the controls. Wipe the panel with a soft, dry cloth and check that no button is stuck. Do not force any button.
3. Reconnect the power and switch the dryer on.
4. Press and hold the child lock button for three seconds to unlock the controls.

If the message returns, leave the dryer switched off and contact Halvard Home support.

Unusual vibration from your Corra induction hob

On the Corra induction hob, E-9865 means the cooling fan is vibrating excessively, usually because its mounting has worked loose. You may notice a rattling sound or feel vibration through the worktop, even after removing your cookware.

Stop cooking and switch the hob off using its controls. Once the cooling fan has stopped, turn off the hob’s electricity supply at the wall isolator. Leave it switched off until it has been checked.

Do not remove the glass surface or try to tighten internal fittings yourself. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection, explaining when the vibration started and whether it continues after cooking. A technician will check the fan mounting and secure or replace it as needed.

Descaling your Vale fridge freezer

A slow or uneven stream from the water dispenser can be caused by limescale blocking the nozzle. KX-3452 is the removable water dispenser nozzle on the Vale fridge freezer.

To descale it:

1. Switch off the fridge freezer at the socket and place a towel beneath the dispenser.
2. Turn the nozzle anticlockwise and gently pull it free.
3. Soak the nozzle for 15 minutes in equal amounts of white vinegar and warm water.
4. Rinse thoroughly with clean water, then refit it by turning clockwise until secure.
5. Restore power and dispense one litre of water into a jug. Discard this water.

Do not pour descaler into the fridge or its cooling system. If the flow remains weak, contact Halvard Home support.

Ordering a spare Mira side brush

If your Mira robot vacuum leaves crumbs along skirting boards, check the side brush. Bent or broken bristles can stop it sweeping dirt into the suction path.

For the Mira robot vacuum, KX-3542 is the part number for the replacement side brush. To order one, contact Halvard Home customer support and quote this part number. Say that you need a side brush for a Mira robot vacuum, and provide your delivery address. Ask support to confirm the price and availability before paying.

Switch the vacuum off before inspecting the brush. Remove any tangled hair first: if the bristles are intact and the brush turns freely afterwards, you may not need a replacement.

Flashing warning light on your Vale fridge freezer

On the Halvard Home Vale fridge freezer, a warning light that flashes twice, pauses, then repeats means the freezer door sensor is not detecting a closed door. KX-3252 is the part number for this sensor.

First, check that drawers and food packets are not stopping the door from closing. Wipe the door seal with a damp cloth, then close the door firmly. Allow two minutes for the warning light to stop flashing.

If the light keeps flashing with the door fully closed, the sensor may be faulty. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection. Do not remove or replace the sensor yourself. Keep the door closed as much as possible while awaiting help.

Mira robot vacuum making a strange noise

On the Mira robot vacuum, E-3873 means the main brush is struggling to turn because hair, thread or another object is caught around it. This can cause a rattling, clicking or grinding noise during cleaning.

Stop the cleaning cycle, switch the vacuum off and remove it from its charging dock. Turn it upside down on a soft cloth. Open the main brush cover and lift out the brush. Gently remove anything wrapped around the brush, checking both ends for trapped debris.

Refit the brush and secure the cover before switching the vacuum on. Try a short clean on a clear floor.

If the noise continues, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support.

Cleaning the Ashby tumble dryer filter

On the Halvard Home Ashby tumble dryer, E-3837 means fluff has blocked the filter enough to restrict airflow. Clean the filter before starting another drying cycle.

1. Switch off the dryer, unplug it and allow it to cool.
2. Open the door and lift the fluff filter out of its slot.
3. Remove fluff from both sides using your fingers or a soft brush.
4. If residue remains, rinse the filter under lukewarm water. Do not use abrasive cleaners.
5. Let the filter dry completely, then refit it securely.

Reconnect the dryer and try a cycle. Never run it without the filter fitted. Clean the filter after every load to help prevent blockages. If the warning returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.

Fenwick cooker hood: interrupted firmware update

On the Fenwick cooker hood, E-3173 means the firmware download was interrupted before installation could begin. The hood keeps its existing firmware, so you can still use the fan and lights.

To try the update again:

1. Check that your home Wi-Fi is working and that the hood is connected.
2. Open the Halvard Home app and select your cooker hood.
3. Tap **Settings**, then **Firmware update**, then **Retry**.

Leave the hood connected to the mains throughout the update. Do not switch it off at the wall while installation is running.

If the download fails again, close and reopen the app, then retry once. If it still fails, contact Halvard Home support and describe the interrupted download.

Corra induction hob: first installation

Before using your Corra induction hob, ask a qualified installer to check that it sits level in the worktop and that its electrical connection is safe.

KX-7011 is the sealing strip supplied for fitting beneath the hob’s glass edge. It must lie flat all the way round before the hob is lowered into place.

During first installation, a folded sealing strip can leave one corner raised, causing the hob to rock when touched. If you notice this, leave the power switched off and ask your installer to lift the hob and refit the strip correctly.

Do not press the raised corner down or add sealant to fill the gap. Only use the hob once the installer has corrected the fit.

Saving energy with your Ashby tumble dryer

Choose Eco for everyday cotton loads and select Cupboard Dry rather than Extra Dry when you do not need additional drying. Spin washing thoroughly before loading, and clean the lint filter after every cycle to maintain airflow.

KX-0711 is the Ashby tumble dryer’s moisture sensor. It helps automatic programmes stop when your clothes reach the selected dryness level. A faulty sensor can make the dryer continue heating after the load is dry, wasting electricity.

If clothes are already dry but the programme repeatedly continues heating, stop the dryer and switch it off at the socket. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange a sensor check. Do not remove panels or attempt to replace the sensor yourself.

Vale fridge freezer display stays blank

If your Vale fridge freezer is still cooling but its display stays blank, the display control board may have failed. KX-8011 is the display control board for this product; a fault in its internal power circuit can stop the screen lighting up without stopping cooling.

Check that the plug is secure and the wall socket is switched on. Switch off and unplug the appliance for five minutes, then reconnect it with dry hands. Allow two minutes for the display to restart.

If the screen remains blank, contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection and, if needed, a board replacement. Do not remove any covers or attempt electrical repairs yourself.

Tessa dishwasher warranty period

Your Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher has a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. It covers manufacturing faults during normal household use, but not accidental damage or faults caused by incorrect installation.

E-4805 means the dishwasher’s digital warranty record is missing its purchase date, so your cover cannot be confirmed automatically. This does not mean your warranty has expired.

Find your receipt or order confirmation, then contact Halvard Home customer support with the purchase date and your dishwasher’s serial number. Support can check your proof of purchase and correct the warranty record.

You do not need to reset the dishwasher to resolve this record fault. Keep your proof of purchase for any future warranty claim.

Booking an Orrin engineer visit

On the Halvard Home Orrin heat pump, E-4085 means the outdoor coil temperature sensor is not sending a reading. The heat pump pauses heating because it cannot safely control defrosting. This fault needs an engineer’s inspection.

Turn heating off at the controller and contact Halvard Home customer support to book a visit. Have your model name, installation address and a description of when the fault appeared ready. Tell the adviser if the heat pump is your only source of heating or hot water.

Do not remove the outdoor unit’s cover or try to reconnect wiring. Before the appointment, clear access to both the outdoor unit and indoor controls. Ask the adviser to confirm any call-out charge before accepting the booking.

articles.topic: the door or lid not closing
articles.text:
Tessa dishwasher door will not close

On your Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, E-4875 means the door latch has not fully engaged, so the machine cannot start a wash.

Switch the dishwasher off before checking the door. Pull out both baskets and reposition any plates, pan handles or utensils sticking beyond their edges. Push the baskets fully back into place: a basket left slightly forward can prevent the door from reaching the latch.

Check the rubber door seal for trapped food and wipe it with a soft, damp cloth. Then close the door gently until you hear a click.

Do not slam the door or force the latch. If the door still will not click shut, leave the dishwasher switched off and contact Halvard Home support for a repair.

Installing your Mira robot vacuum

For the Mira robot vacuum, KX-1639 is the part number of the supplied charging dock. Place this dock against a wall on a level floor, leaving at least one metre of clear space in front. Connect the power lead and switch on the wall socket.

If the vacuum does not begin charging during first installation, a clear transport strip may still be covering its charging contacts. This prevents the vacuum from making an electrical connection with the dock.

Switch off the vacuum and unplug the dock. Remove the strip from the contacts underneath the vacuum, then reconnect the dock and switch the vacuum on. Place it on the dock and check that the charging indicator lights up.

Orrin heat pump display stays blank

If your Orrin heat pump display stays blank, first check that the wall isolator is switched on and that your home’s circuit breaker has not tripped.

Switch the heat pump off at the wall isolator, wait 60 seconds, then switch it on again. If the circuit breaker trips again, leave the heat pump switched off and contact a qualified electrician.

A loose connection in the display power module can stop electricity reaching the screen. KX-1693 is the replacement display power module for this product.

If the display remains blank after restarting, contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection. A technician should check the connection and replace the module if needed. Do not remove the casing yourself.

Replacing a damaged lint filter

KX-3639 is the replacement lint filter for the Halvard Home Ashby tumble dryer. If the filter mesh is torn, lint can pass into the dryer’s airflow system. Stop using the dryer until the damaged filter has been replaced.

Switch off the dryer, unplug it and allow it to cool. Open the door and lift the lint filter out of its slot in the door opening. Remove loose lint from the slot with a soft brush, then slide the replacement filter fully into place. Do not force it.

Order the replacement from Halvard Home support, quoting the part number above and your dryer’s model name. Clean the new filter after every drying cycle, and never run the dryer without it fitted.

Ordering a spare Brio kettle lid

E-6736 means your Brio kettle’s lid locking clip is not holding the lid securely shut. If the clip is cracked or broken, you will need a replacement lid.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely before checking the clip. Do not try to hold the lid closed while boiling or repair the clip with glue.

To order a spare lid, contact Halvard Home customer support with the model name and serial number printed on the kettle’s base. Ask for a replacement lid for your Brio kettle, and confirm compatibility and the total price before paying.

Fit the new lid following its supplied instructions. Stop using the kettle if the lid still will not lock securely.

Orrin heat pump: first installation warning

On a newly installed Halvard Home Orrin heat pump, E-6763 means air remains trapped in the heating circuit, preventing steady water flow during commissioning. The unit pauses heating to protect itself.

Leave the heat pump switched off using its normal power control and contact your installer. Ask them to complete the heating circuit purge, check that the isolation valves are fully open, and confirm that water flows correctly before restarting commissioning.

Do not remove the casing, loosen pipe connections or repeatedly restart the unit. Purging the circuit is an installer task, not a routine customer reset.

Once the installer has cleared the trapped air, they should restart commissioning and check that the warning does not return.

Tessa dishwasher not switching on

On the Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, E-1736 means the power protection circuit has shut the unit down after detecting an unstable mains supply. The display may briefly show the code before going blank.

To reset the dishwasher:

1. Switch off the wall socket and unplug the dishwasher with dry hands.
2. Leave it disconnected for 10 minutes.
3. Check that the plug and cable have no visible damage.
4. If they look undamaged, reconnect the dishwasher directly to the wall socket, switch the socket on, then press the power button.

Do not use an extension lead. If the dishwasher remains unresponsive or the fault returns, unplug it and contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove any panels or attempt internal repairs.

Lumen thermostat making a buzzing noise

A brief click when heating starts or stops is normal. A continuous buzz lasting more than 10 seconds can indicate a loose coil inside the heating relay module.

KX-9495 is the part number for this module in the Lumen smart thermostat. The loose coil vibrates while the relay is powered, causing the unusual noise.

Turn the heating off using the thermostat, then switch off power to the heating system at its labelled isolation switch. Do not remove the thermostat cover or try to tighten internal components.

Contact Halvard Home support and describe when the buzzing occurs. A qualified heating engineer should inspect the relay module and replace it if the loose-coil fault is confirmed.

Water leaking underneath your Corra induction hob

Water beneath your Corra induction hob can be caused by a split perimeter seal. KX-9945 is the seal that sits between the hob’s glass edge and the worktop; if it splits, spilled water can pass into the cupboard below.

Switch the hob off and isolate its electricity supply at the consumer unit before wiping up any water. Use dry hands and do not touch wet switches or wiring. Do not use the hob again until it has been checked.

Once the surface is cool, wipe away standing water without lifting the hob or removing its covers. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange inspection and seal replacement by a qualified technician. Explain that water appears beneath the hob after spills.

Pairing your Lumen with a voice assistant

If your voice assistant cannot find your Lumen smart thermostat, its saved account link may have expired. This pairing fault prevents voice control, but you can still adjust the temperature on the thermostat.

KX-9491 is the part number for the thermostat’s wireless pairing module. You do not need to remove or replace it to refresh the account link.

To reconnect, open your voice assistant’s app and unlink your Halvard Home account. Wait 60 seconds, then link the account again and search for devices. Keep the thermostat connected to your home Wi-Fi throughout.

If pairing still fails, contact Halvard Home support and quote the module’s part number. Do not open the thermostat casing.

Corra induction hob: frost or condensation

On the Corra induction hob, E-3293 means the moisture sensor has detected condensation beneath the control panel and stopped heating as a precaution. This can happen when warm, damp air meets a very cold hob.

Switch the hob off at its wall isolator and leave it for at least 30 minutes. Wipe visible surface moisture with a soft, dry cloth. If there is frost, let it melt naturally, then dry the glass. Do not use a hairdryer, hot water or a scraper to speed up thawing.

Restore power only when the surface is dry and frost-free. If the warning returns, switch off the hob and contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

Replacing the Brio kettle’s filter

On the Halvard Home Brio kettle, E-2393 means the removable limescale filter is not engaging its safety switch, usually because the filter’s retaining clip is damaged. The kettle will not heat until the filter is securely fitted.

Unplug the kettle, empty it carefully and leave it to cool for 15 minutes. Open the lid and check the filter behind the spout. If the clip is cracked or missing, replace the complete filter rather than trying to glue it.

Order a replacement filter for the Brio kettle from Halvard Home support. Slide the new filter into its guides and press gently until it clicks into place.

If the warning remains, stop using the kettle and contact support.

# Fenwick cooker hood: strange noise during use

A rattling or grinding noise with E-3223 means your Fenwick cooker hood has detected resistance at the fan, usually caused by something obstructing its movement.

Switch the hood off and isolate it from the electricity supply before checking it. Wait ten minutes for it to cool.

Remove the grease filters as described in your user guide. Check for loose debris around the filter opening, but do not reach into the fan or remove internal covers. Refit the filters securely, as a loose filter can also vibrate during use.

Restore power and briefly test the hood on its lowest speed. If the noise or warning returns, switch it off and contact Halvard Home support. Do not continue using it.

Mira stops charging after a power cut

If your Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum was cleaning when the power went off, it may return to its dock but fail to charge once power is restored.

KX-8033 is the dock’s power protection module. A sudden loss of mains power can leave this module in its protective shutdown state, preventing the dock from supplying charge.

Switch off the vacuum and unplug the dock from the wall socket for 60 seconds. Then plug the dock back in, switch on the vacuum and place it on the charging contacts.

If charging does not start, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the dock or attempt to replace the module yourself.

Weak extraction from your Fenwick cooker hood

If your Fenwick cooker hood runs but removes steam slowly, its grease filter may be clogged. A build-up of cooking grease blocks airflow, making extraction feel weak even at the highest fan setting.

KX-8303 is the washable metal grease filter for this cooker hood. Clean it to restore airflow:

- Switch off the hood and isolate it from the electricity supply.
- Support the filter, release its retaining catch and lower it carefully.
- Soak it in warm water with washing-up liquid for 10 minutes, then gently brush away grease.
- Rinse and let it dry completely before refitting.

Restore power and test the fan. If extraction remains weak, contact Halvard Home support for further checks.

Cleaning the Mira robot vacuum filter

If your Mira robot vacuum leaves dust behind despite an empty dust bin, a clogged filter may be reducing suction.

Switch off the vacuum and remove it from its charging dock. Take out the dust bin, open its lid and lift out the filter. Empty the bin, then gently tap the filter over a rubbish bin to loosen trapped dust. Use a soft, dry brush to remove fluff from the filter surface. Do not wash the filter or refit it while damp.

Check for tears or damaged edges. If damaged, replace it with KX-8038, the replacement filter for the Mira robot vacuum. Refit the filter securely before closing the bin and restarting the vacuum.

Orrin heat pump warranty period

Your Halvard Home Orrin heat pump has a five-year warranty from the installation date, covering manufacturing faults in parts and labour.

If the display shows E-7160, the heat pump’s warranty record is missing its installation date, so the system cannot confirm the remaining warranty period. This is a registration fault, not a heating fault, and does not automatically mean your cover has expired.

Find your installation certificate or dated installer’s invoice, then contact Halvard Home support to have the warranty record corrected. Keep a copy of the document for future claims.

You can continue using the heat pump normally while the record is updated. Do not change the installation date yourself or reset the unit to clear the message.

Booking an engineer for your Vale fridge freezer

On the Vale fridge freezer, E-7610 means the freezer temperature sensor has failed, so the appliance cannot reliably control freezer cooling. This fault needs an engineer visit; changing the temperature setting will not fix it.

Contact Halvard Home customer support to request a repair appointment. Have your appliance’s serial number, purchase date, postcode and a description of the fault ready. Tell the adviser whether frozen food has started to soften.

Keep the freezer door closed as much as possible. If food is softening, move it to another working freezer rather than waiting for the visit.

Before the engineer arrives, clear the area around the appliance so they can reach it safely. Do not remove any panels yourself.

Vale fridge freezer cooling slowly

On the Vale fridge freezer, E-7190 means the freezer’s air circulation fan is running too slowly, reducing the flow of cold air and weakening cooling.

Check that food packets are not covering the air vents inside either compartment. Leave a clear gap around each vent, and make sure both doors close fully.

Set the fridge to 4°C and the freezer to −18°C. Keep the doors closed as much as possible and allow six hours for cooling to improve.

If the warning remains or returns, contact Halvard Home support to arrange a fan inspection. Do not remove internal panels or try to turn the fan yourself. Move perishable food to another working fridge if it is no longer staying cold.

Pairing your Ashby dryer with a voice assistant

Part number KX-9996 identifies the voice connection module in your Ashby tumble dryer. A pairing fault can leave this module stuck in setup mode, so your voice assistant cannot find the dryer.

To reset the connection, stop any drying programme and switch the dryer off at the wall for 30 seconds. Switch it back on, then hold the Wi-Fi button for five seconds until its light flashes.

Open the Halvard Home app and follow the prompts to reconnect your dryer. In your voice assistant’s app, enable Halvard Home, link your account and search for devices again.

If the dryer still does not appear, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the casing or try to replace the module yourself.

Resetting your Vale fridge freezer

KX-9969 is the control panel module in your Vale fridge freezer. A stored-settings fault in this module can leave Holiday mode active even after you switch it off. Resetting to factory settings clears the saved preferences and may resolve this fault.

To reset:
1. Keep the appliance connected to the power supply.
2. Press and hold the Settings button for 10 seconds, until the display flashes.
3. Release the button and wait one minute before using the controls.

The reset restores the fridge setting to 4°C and the freezer setting to −18°C. Actual temperatures will take time to adjust.

If Holiday mode remains active, contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove or replace the control panel yourself.

Vale fridge freezer: first installation

If the freezer door will not close fully during first installation, a transit spacer may still be fitted beneath the door.

KX-9696 is the removable transit spacer supplied with your Vale fridge freezer to hold the freezer door steady during delivery. It is packaging, not a working appliance component, and must be removed before use.

With the appliance unplugged, open the freezer door and gently pull the spacer out by hand. Do not use sharp tools or force it. Close the door and check that the seal touches the cabinet all the way round.

If the spacer will not release, leave the appliance unplugged and contact Halvard Home support. Follow the installation guide before switching on.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Fan speed signal fault

On the Halvard Home Fenwick cooker hood, E-1216 means the control board cannot detect the fan motor’s speed. The hood stops the fan to prevent it running without speed monitoring.

To reset the hood, turn it off using its controls, then switch off its power at the wall for five minutes. Restore the power and select the lowest fan setting.

If the message clears and the fan runs normally, you can use the hood again. If the message returns, or the fan hums without turning, switch off the power and contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove the motor cover or try to repair internal wiring.

Burning smell from your Orrin heat pump

On the Halvard Home Orrin heat pump, E-1261 means the outdoor fan motor has overheated, potentially scorching its electrical insulation and causing a burning smell.

Stop using the heat pump immediately. If there is no smoke or fire and it is safe to approach, switch it off at the controller, then disconnect its power using the labelled isolation switch. Switching off at the controller alone does not isolate the electricity.

Do not restart the unit, remove its covers or attempt repairs. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection by a qualified engineer, and describe when the smell started.

If you see smoke or flames, keep away, leave the property and call 999. Do not use water on the appliance.

Flashing warning light on your Fenwick cooker hood

On the Fenwick cooker hood, a flashing warning light with E-0216 means the metal grease filter is blocked, restricting airflow. Clean the filter before using the hood again.

Switch the hood off at the wall and let it cool. Release the filter catch and carefully lower the filter. Soak it in warm water with washing-up liquid for 15 minutes, then gently brush away grease. Rinse thoroughly and leave it to dry completely before refitting it securely.

Restore power, then press and hold the light button for five seconds to reset the warning.

If the warning returns after cleaning, switch the hood off and contact Halvard Home support. Do not run the hood without its grease filter fitted.

Ashby tumble dryer: frost or condensation build-up

Heavy condensation or frost inside your Ashby tumble dryer may be caused by a split condenser housing seal. This fault lets damp air reach cold internal surfaces, where moisture collects and may freeze in an unheated room.

KX-5912 is the replacement condenser housing seal for this product. If moisture repeatedly collects beneath the dryer or frost returns after thawing, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support to arrange inspection and seal replacement if needed.

Switch off and unplug the dryer before wiping any accessible moisture. Leave it unplugged until all visible frost has thawed. Do not remove casing panels or use a hairdryer to melt ice. A technician should replace the seal before you use the dryer again.

Frost or condensation on your Orrin heat pump

A light coating of frost on the outdoor unit is normal in cold weather and should clear during automatic defrosting. Condensation beneath the unit is also normal.

KX-9512 is the condensate drain insert in the Orrin heat pump’s outdoor unit. If this insert becomes blocked with dirt, water can collect in the base and freeze, causing a thick layer of ice.

Switch the heat pump off using its controls and remove loose leaves from around the base, without opening any covers. Do not chip away ice or pour boiling water over the unit.

If thick ice remains or returns, leave the unit switched off and contact Halvard Home support to arrange inspection and cleaning of the drain insert.

Recycling your old Keel washing machine

On the Keel washing machine, KX-5913 identifies the drain pump assembly. A cracked pump housing can cause water to leak beneath the machine during draining.

If you notice this fault, stop using the machine, turn off its water supply and unplug it only if the plug and surrounding area are dry. Ask a qualified repairer to assess it before deciding to recycle it.

If repair is not practical, book an electrical appliance collection through your local council or ask your retailer about removal when buying a replacement. Do not put the machine in household rubbish.

Before collection, remove all laundry and follow the user manual’s draining instructions. Arrange help with disconnection and lifting; do not move the machine alone.

Tessa dishwasher: flashing warning light

On your Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, a flashing warning light with E-4021 means water has not drained within three minutes. A blocked drain filter is the most common cause.

Stop the programme and switch the dishwasher off at the mains. If the water is hot, let it cool before opening the door fully. Place towels around the base to catch any spills.

Remove the bottom basket, then turn the filter anticlockwise and lift it out. Rinse it under warm running water, removing food scraps with a soft brush. Refit the filter securely before restoring power.

Run a rinse programme. If the warning returns or water remains inside, stop using the dishwasher and contact Halvard Home support.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Mira robot vacuum: blocked brush alert

The fault code E-0421 on your Mira robot vacuum means the main brush cannot turn freely. Hair, thread or debris wrapped around the brush is the usual cause.

To clear the fault:

1. Switch off the vacuum and remove it from the charging dock.
2. Turn it upside down on a soft, dry surface.
3. Unclip the main brush cover and lift out the brush.
4. Carefully remove tangled hair and debris, including anything caught around the brush ends.
5. Refit the brush and clip the cover securely into place.

Return the vacuum to the floor, switch it on and start cleaning. If the fault returns, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support.

Keel washing machine: first installation

On your Halvard Home Keel washing machine, E-4020 means the drum is still restrained by one or more transport bolts left in place during installation. These bolts protect the drum during delivery but must be removed before use.

To fix this:

- Stop the programme, switch off the machine and unplug it.
- Check the rear of the machine and remove all transport bolts, following the installation guide.
- Fit the supplied plastic caps into the empty bolt holes.
- Keep the bolts for any future move.

Once the machine is level and its hoses are securely connected, plug it in and run an empty rinse and spin programme. If the warning returns, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Keel washing machine warranty

Your Halvard Home Keel washing machine has a two-year warranty from the delivery date, covering manufacturing faults during normal domestic use. Keep your receipt or order confirmation as proof of purchase.

KX-2446 is the part number for the drain pump fitted to your Keel washing machine. If a manufacturing defect causes the pump housing to crack and leak within the warranty period, Halvard Home will repair or replace the faulty pump free of charge.

Stop using the machine if you notice water leaking underneath it. Switch it off and unplug it only if the plug and surrounding area are dry.

Contact Halvard Home support with your purchase details and a description of the leak. Arrange a warranty assessment before attempting repairs yourself.

Corra induction hob not switching on

If your Corra induction hob has no lights and does not respond to touch, first check that its wall isolator switch is on. Make sure your hands and the control panel are dry.

Switch the hob off at the wall for five minutes, then switch it back on and try the power control again.

A failed internal power supply module can leave the hob completely unresponsive. KX-2464 is the replacement part number for this module in the Corra induction hob.

If the hob still will not switch on, leave it isolated and contact Halvard Home support. Ask for a qualified technician to check the power supply module. Do not open the hob or attempt to replace the module yourself.

Flashing warning light on your Lumen thermostat

A flashing amber warning light on the Halvard Home Lumen smart thermostat means its backup temperature sensor module, part number KX-2456, is not responding. The thermostat pauses scheduled heating because it cannot confirm a safe room temperature.

First, check that the thermostat is firmly seated on its wall mount. Do not remove the mount or touch any wiring. Next, select **Settings**, then **Restart** on the thermostat screen. Wait two minutes for it to reconnect and check the sensor.

If the light stops flashing, your heating schedule will resume automatically. If it continues, leave scheduled heating paused and contact Halvard Home support to arrange a sensor check. Do not attempt to replace the module yourself.

articles.topic: the door or lid not closing
articles.text:
Corra induction hob lid will not close

E-3946 means the Corra induction hob’s lid sensor has detected that the protective lid is not fully closed. A pan handle, food debris or a misaligned hinge can prevent the lid from reaching its closed position.

Switch off the hob and let the cooking surface cool completely before checking it. Remove all cookware, then wipe the lid’s rim and the surrounding edge with a soft, damp cloth. Gently lower the lid without forcing it.

If the lid closes properly, switch the hob off at the wall for one minute, then restore power. If the warning returns, or the lid remains crooked or stuck, contact Halvard Home support. Do not adjust the hinges yourself.

Keep the lid fully open whenever you cook.

Timer or delay start will not run

On the Halvard Home Orrin heat pump, E-3496 means the internal clock has lost its time setting, so the unit cannot calculate when a timed or delayed start should begin. This can happen after a power cut.

To restore the timer:

1. Open Settings on the control panel and select Clock.
2. Set the current day and time, then press Save.
3. Cancel the existing timer or delayed start.
4. Enter a new start time and confirm it.

Choose a start time at least five minutes ahead when testing the timer. The heat pump should remain on standby until that time.

If the warning returns after saving the clock, contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove the unit’s casing.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Orrin heat pump display fault

On the Halvard Home Orrin heat pump, E-5946 means the outdoor coil temperature sensor is not providing a reliable reading. The heat pump stops its compressor because it cannot safely control the defrost cycle.

Switch the heat pump off using its controller, then turn off the power at the isolator. Leave it off for five minutes before restoring power and restarting it once.

If the fault returns, leave the unit switched off and contact Halvard Home support or a qualified heat pump engineer. Tell them that the outdoor coil sensor fault has returned after a restart.

Do not remove the casing, touch internal wiring or repeatedly reset the unit. The sensor and its connections need professional inspection.

Booking an engineer for your Corra induction hob

If your Corra induction hob switches off during cooking and its cooling fan stays silent, the fan may have failed. Stop using the hob and switch it off at the wall before booking an engineer visit.

KX-5646 is the replacement cooling fan for the Corra induction hob, not an error code. An engineer must confirm the fault and fit the part; do not open the hob yourself.

Contact Halvard Home customer support to arrange a visit. Have your hob’s serial number, purchase date and a description of the fault ready. Mention the suspected cooling fan problem so the team can plan the repair. Ask about call-out charges and warranty cover before confirming your appointment.

Saving energy on your Mira

To reduce electricity use, open the Mira app, select Settings, then Power, and switch on Energy Saving. This setting reduces standby power after the battery finishes charging. Use Eco suction for everyday dust, and schedule cleaning only as often as your home needs it.

Once charging is complete, the robot’s power light should dim within 10 minutes. If it stays bright and the fan continues running, the standby power module may be faulty, preventing energy-saving mode from starting.

KX-5664 is the replacement standby power module for the Mira robot vacuum. If these symptoms persist after restarting the robot, contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection and replacement if needed. Do not open the robot or replace the module yourself.

articles.topic: the door or lid not closing
articles.text:
Keel washing machine door will not close

If your Keel washing machine door bounces back instead of clicking shut, the door latch may be stuck in its closed position.

Switch off the machine and unplug it before checking the door. Remove any clothing trapped between the door and the rubber seal, then wipe away visible fluff around the latch opening. Try closing the door gently once. Do not slam it or push tools into the latch.

KX-5546 is the replacement door latch assembly for the Keel washing machine. If the latch remains stuck and the door still will not close, leave the machine unplugged and contact Halvard Home support to arrange replacement by a qualified technician.

Corra induction hob heating slowly

If your Corra induction hob heats slowly or feels weak, E-6779 means restricted cooling airflow has triggered the hob’s protective power limit. The hob reduces heat output to prevent its internal electronics from overheating.

Switch off all cooking zones, then turn off the hob at its wall isolation switch. Leave it to cool for 20 minutes. Once cool, check that items in the cupboard or drawer beneath the hob are not blocking its ventilation openings. Move any obstructions away, but do not remove covers or reach inside the appliance.

Restore power and test one zone with an induction-compatible pan containing water. If heating remains weak or the warning returns, switch the hob off and contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection.

Recycling your Mira robot vacuum

On the Mira robot vacuum, E-7679 means the battery has reached the end of its safe charging life. Stop using the vacuum, switch it off and unplug its charging dock from the mains. Do not try to recharge it.

Contact Halvard Home support to check whether a battery replacement is suitable before recycling the whole unit.

If you are disposing of your Mira, take it to a local household waste recycling centre that accepts electrical appliances. Never put the vacuum or its battery in household rubbish or kerbside recycling.

Leave the battery inside the vacuum unless a qualified technician removes it. Tell recycling centre staff about the battery fault so they can arrange appropriate handling.

Recycling your Brio kettle

On the Halvard Home Brio kettle, E-6770 means the internal electrical insulation has failed, making the kettle unsafe to use. Stop using it immediately and unplug it from the wall. Do not switch it on again or try to open the casing.

If you are retiring the kettle, let it cool completely, then empty out any water. Take both the kettle and its power base to a recycling centre that accepts small electrical appliances. Keep the cable attached.

Do not put the kettle in your household rubbish or mixed recycling bin. Your local council can tell you where to find an electrical recycling collection point. Check opening times and whether you need to book before travelling.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Lumen thermostat: room sensor fault

If your Lumen smart thermostat displays KX-7896, it is flagging a fault with the room temperature sensor module identified by that part number. This means the thermostat cannot get a reliable temperature reading, so it pauses automatic heating control.

Switch off power to the thermostat at its labelled isolation switch for 60 seconds, then switch it back on. Wait two minutes for the display to restart and check whether the warning clears.

If the warning returns, contact Halvard Home support and describe what appears on the screen. Do not remove the thermostat cover or attempt to replace the sensor yourself. A qualified technician should inspect the module and its connections.

articles.topic: the door or lid not closing
articles.text:
Ashby tumble dryer door not closing

If your Ashby tumble dryer door will not close, switch the dryer off and unplug it before checking the opening. Remove any clothing trapped between the door and the seal, then wipe away fluff with a soft, dry cloth.

On this product, KX-7986 is the door catch that holds the door shut. A cracked catch can stop the door clicking into place, even when the opening is clear.

Check the catch for visible cracks or a loose edge. If it is damaged, do not force the door or try to hold it closed with tape. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange a replacement catch and fitting. Do not use the dryer until the door closes securely.

Connecting your Keel washing machine to wi-fi

Your Halvard Home Keel washing machine connects to a 2.4 GHz home wi-fi network. If your router combines network bands, select its separate 2.4 GHz network during setup.

A connection fault can occur when the machine retains an old network password after you change your router settings. To clear the saved connection, switch the machine on and hold the Wi-Fi button for five seconds, until its light flashes. Then repeat setup in the Halvard Home app using your current password.

KX-7856 is the part number for this product’s internal wi-fi module, not an error message. If the Wi-Fi light remains off after resetting, contact Halvard Home support for assessment. Do not open the machine or replace the module yourself.

Mira robot vacuum not switching on

For the Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum, E-9454 means the battery protection system has blocked startup because the battery charge is too low.

To restore power:

1. Plug the charging dock into a working wall socket and switch the socket on.
2. Unplug the dock before wiping its charging contacts and those underneath the vacuum with a dry cloth.
3. Reconnect the dock, then place the vacuum on it with the charging contacts aligned.
4. Leave it charging for three hours, then press and hold the vacuum’s power button for three seconds.

If the vacuum still will not switch on, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the battery compartment or attempt to bypass the protection system.

Saving energy with your Tessa dishwasher

The Tessa dishwasher’s Eco programme uses lower wash temperatures and a longer cycle to reduce electricity use. For everyday loads, select Eco and wait until the dishwasher is full before starting, without blocking the spray arms.

Error code E-9544 means the temperature sensor has detected overheating during Eco mode, so the dishwasher has paused the programme to prevent unnecessary energy use.

Switch the dishwasher off at the mains for five minutes, then restore power and select Eco again. If the warning returns, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support to arrange a sensor check. Do not remove any panels or attempt repairs yourself.

For further savings, switch off heated drying if your model offers this option.

Burning smell from your Tessa dishwasher

On the Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, E-9474 means the heater’s electrical connection has overheated. This can produce a burning plastic smell, and the dishwasher must not be used until it has been checked.

Stop the programme and switch the dishwasher off. If it is safe to do so, disconnect the power at the wall socket or the household circuit breaker. Do not touch a plug or socket that feels hot, looks damaged or is wet.

Do not restart the dishwasher, remove panels or attempt to repair the wiring. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange a qualified service visit, and describe the smell.

If you see smoke or flames, leave the area and call the fire service.

Cleaning the Tessa dishwasher filter

Food trapped in the filter can cause water to pool at the bottom of your Tessa dishwasher after a wash.

KX-8645 is the part number for this dishwasher’s removable filter. Clean it once a week to help prevent blockages.

Switch off and unplug the dishwasher, then let it cool. Pull out the lower basket. Turn the filter anticlockwise and lift it out from the bottom of the tub.

Rinse the filter under warm running water, using a soft brush to remove food and grease. Avoid wire brushes, which can damage the mesh.

Refit the filter and turn it clockwise until secure. Never run the dishwasher without it. If water still pools after cleaning, contact Halvard Home support.

Replacing a damaged Fenwick cooker hood filter

If the grease filter no longer sits flush beneath your Fenwick cooker hood, its frame may be bent. A gap around the frame lets greasy air pass around the mesh rather than through it.

KX-8465 is the replacement metal grease filter for this product. Replace the filter if its frame is bent or its mesh is torn.

Switch off the hood at the wall and allow it to cool. Support the old filter with one hand, release its retaining latch and lower it carefully. Fit the replacement into the rear slots, then raise it until the latch clicks shut.

Check that the filter sits flat and is secure before restoring power. Contact Halvard Home support to order a replacement.

Burning smell from your Vale fridge freezer

KX-2645 is the compressor start relay in your Vale fridge freezer. Overheated contacts inside this part can cause a burning smell near the back of the appliance.

Stop using the fridge freezer immediately. Switch it off at the wall and unplug it only if the plug and socket are safe to touch. Do not restart it to check whether the smell has gone.

Contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection by a qualified technician. The relay may need replacing; do not remove covers or attempt the repair yourself.

Keep the doors closed while arranging alternative cold storage for your food. If you see smoke or flames, move away, leave the property and call 999.

articles.topic: using it in a holiday home
articles.text:
Using your Lumen thermostat in a holiday home

On the Halvard Home Lumen smart thermostat, E-8255 means the holiday schedule has no return date, so holiday mode cannot start. Your existing heating schedule stays active until you correct this.

To fix it, open the thermostat’s menu, select Holiday, and enter the date and time when you next expect to arrive. Choose your holiday temperature, then select Save. Check that the display shows both your return date and that holiday mode is active before leaving.

If your plans change, update the return date rather than switching the thermostat off. Keep the heating system powered so it can maintain your chosen temperature while the property is empty.

If the warning remains, contact Halvard Home support.

Burning smell from your Fenwick cooker hood

On the Fenwick cooker hood, E-8525 means the fan motor has overheated, which can cause a burning smell. Stop cooking, turn the hood off and isolate its electricity supply at the wall switch, if safe to do so.

Do not restart the hood to check whether the smell has cleared. Keep it switched off until a qualified service engineer has inspected it.

Once the hood is completely cool, check the removable grease filters for heavy build-up. Grease can restrict airflow and contribute to overheating. Clean the filters according to the user guide, but do not remove electrical covers or attempt to repair the motor.

If you see smoke or flames, leave the area and call the fire service.

articles.topic: using it in a holiday home
articles.text:
Using Mira in a holiday home

If your holiday home has been left unheated, your Mira robot vacuum may display E-8250. This means the battery is too cold to charge safely, so charging has been paused.

Switch off the vacuum and unplug its charging base. Move both into a dry room at 15–25°C and leave them for at least two hours before reconnecting the base and placing Mira on it. Do not use a radiator, hairdryer or other direct heat source to warm the vacuum.

Once the warning clears, let Mira charge before starting a clean. Before leaving the property empty again, store it somewhere dry and frost-free. If the warning remains after warming and reconnecting, contact Halvard Home support.

Pairing your Brio kettle with a voice assistant

KX-3056 is the part number for the Brio kettle’s wireless pairing module. This module lets the kettle connect to the Halvard Home app so you can link a supported voice assistant.

A stalled pairing session can leave the kettle visible in the app but unavailable to your voice assistant, particularly after a router restart.

To reconnect:

1. Connect your phone to your home’s 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.
2. Hold the kettle’s pairing button for five seconds, until the wireless light flashes.
3. Open the Halvard Home app and add the kettle again.
4. In the app’s Voice assistants menu, select your assistant and follow the linking instructions.

If pairing still fails, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the kettle or replace the module yourself.

Connecting your Mira to home wi-fi

KX-0356 is the part number for Mira’s wi-fi module, which connects the vacuum to your router. A pairing fault can leave the module searching for your old network after you replace your router.

To reconnect your Mira:

1. Connect your phone to your home’s 2.4 GHz wi-fi network. Mira cannot connect to a 5 GHz-only network.
2. Place the vacuum on its charging dock near the router.
3. Open the Halvard Home app, select your Mira and choose **Wi-fi settings**, then **Change network**.
4. Enter your new wi-fi password and follow the pairing instructions.

If pairing still fails, restart your router and try again. Contact Halvard Home support if Mira keeps searching for the old network; do not open the vacuum.

Updating your Brio kettle’s firmware

If a firmware update stops before completion, the kettle’s wireless connection may have dropped. This can leave the app showing ‘Updating’ even though no progress is being made.

KX-3356 is the Brio kettle’s wireless control module, which receives firmware updates. If updating repeatedly fails, contact Halvard Home support to have this module checked; do not open the kettle yourself.

To retry the update:

- Let the kettle cool, empty it and place it on its powered base.
- Connect your phone to the same home Wi-Fi network as the kettle.
- Open the Halvard Home app, select your kettle, then choose ‘Firmware update’.
- Keep the kettle powered and your phone nearby until the app confirms completion.

Do not boil water during the update.

Brio kettle: first installation

Before using your Brio kettle, remove all packaging and place the power base on a dry, level worktop.

During first installation, E-5328 means the kettle is not seated correctly on its base. A protective packing insert left beneath the kettle can cause this fault.

To fix it, switch off the socket and unplug the base. Lift off the kettle, remove any remaining packing material and check that both contact surfaces are dry. Put the kettle squarely back on the base, then reconnect the power.

Rinse the kettle, fill it to the MAX mark with fresh cold water, boil once and discard the water before making drinks.

If the warning returns, unplug the kettle and contact Halvard Home support.

articles.topic: using it in a holiday home
articles.text:
Corra hob: condensation in a holiday home

On the Corra induction hob, E-5238 means condensation is interfering with the touch controls. This can happen when a cold holiday home is heated quickly, leaving moisture on the glass.

Switch the hob off at its wall isolator. Once the cooking surface is cool, wipe the glass and control area with a clean, dry cloth. Ventilate the room and leave the hob switched off for at least two hours so any remaining moisture can evaporate. Do not use a hairdryer or heater to dry it.

Restore power and try the hob again. If the warning returns, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. If you are a guest, tell the property owner or manager.

Vale fridge freezer warranty period

Your Halvard Home Vale fridge freezer comes with a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. Keep your receipt or order confirmation as proof of when cover began.

On this model, E-5338 means the purchase date is missing from the appliance’s warranty record, preventing it from displaying the correct warranty end date. This is a registration fault, not a cooling fault, and does not itself mean your warranty has expired.

Contact Halvard Home support with your proof of purchase and ask for the warranty record to be corrected. There is no need to unplug the appliance or change its temperature settings for this message.

Your warranty does not affect your statutory rights.

Moving your Tessa dishwasher

Before moving your Tessa dishwasher, switch it off, unplug it and turn off the water supply. Disconnect the inlet and drain hoses, catching any remaining water in a shallow tray.

KX-8618 is the rear transport clip that holds the drain hose against the dishwasher during a move. Secure the hose in this clip before lifting. If the clip is cracked, contact Halvard Home for a replacement before transporting the unit.

Keep the dishwasher upright and use two people to move it. Never lift it by the door handle.

After positioning it, release the drain hose from the clip and reconnect it without bends or trapped sections. Failure to drain after moving may be caused by a hose crushed beneath the cabinet. Check its route before running a programme.

Water leaking underneath your Lumen thermostat

Water beneath your Lumen smart thermostat can be caused by a split cable-entry seal. This lets warm, damp air reach the cold wall behind the thermostat, where moisture forms and drips from the lower edge.

KX-6818 is the replacement cable-entry seal for this product, not an error message.

If you notice dripping:

- Do not touch the thermostat while it is wet.
- Switch off the heating controls at their electrical isolator, provided the switch and surrounding area are dry.
- Contact Halvard Home support or a qualified heating engineer to inspect the seal and replace it if damaged.

Ask the engineer to check for nearby pipe leaks too. Do not restore power until the thermostat has been checked and declared safe.

Ordering a replacement drying rack
